entries.claim: Stage 1 trains, per dataset, a single-frame autoencoder that splits the dense contact map C into a structure-oriented latent z (shaped by its own reconstruction and by a relational loss that matches pairwise z distances to R2 + wrench teacher distances) and a complementary code r that only adds a residual correction on top of the z-only map; the r branch reads z through a stop-gradient and no independence term is used.
entries.metric: Architecture description (no metric). For the redrawn diagram: C (512 values, one per canonical surface point) and geometry G -> E_z (point transformer over 512 tokens [geo | C], conditioned on G, 4 attention-pool queries) -> z; D_z (geometry tokens only, conditioned on [G | z]) -> z-only map C_bar; E_r (tokens [geo | C | 10 x (C - sg(C_bar))], conditioned on [G | sg(z)]) -> r; D_r (tokens [geo | sg(C_bar)], conditioned on [G | sg(z) | r], output = per-point scalar readout + a structure-conditioned 64-D linear basis combined by r) -> Delta_C; C_hat = C_bar + Delta_C. Losses: L_coarse = MSE(C_bar, C) -> E_z, D_z; L_rel = SmoothL1 between batch-normalised pairwise distances of z and of the teacher (1/2 R2-descriptor distance + 1/2 wrench-profile distance) over the 8128 pairs of a 128-frame batch -> z only; L_full = MSE(C_hat, C) -> E_r, D_r and, through C_bar, the z branch; 0.01 x mean|Delta_C| -> r branch. Phase A trains the z branch alone, phase B adds the r branch (z frozen 3000 steps, 0.1 x lr 3000 steps, then joint).

both | A0 plain autoencoder: latent h /.locator: row model=A0; columns latent_h, relational_loss, residual_branch, n_params

caveats: z is taught, not found unsupervised: the only thing that makes z structural is the relational R2 + wrench teacher; no network output is compared with R2 and no independence, mutual-information, adversarial or orthogonality loss is used (sanity checks 15 and 16).
r is conditional on z by design (E_r and D_r both read z and the z-only map), so the claim under test is role separation, not independence (report Section 3, H4).
Single-frame representation experiment: nothing temporal is trained; trajectories are used only at evaluation time.

The existing fig1_architecture.png carries stale text (zero-init output, lambda_delta 0.05, 0.1 x lr for 2k steps); the final recipe is non-zero FiLM gates, lambda_delta 0.01, 3000 frozen + 3000 slow steps.
The residual branch needed three failed launches before it activated; the reported r is the r of one specific decoder recipe (report Sections 13 and 15).

The primary A2 / A3 phase B started from the z branch of an earlier 16 000-step launch (training logs: 'z branch initialised from A3_seed0_phaseA (16000 steps)'), although report Section 6 also says the runs are from scratch.
Bottleneck variants with a 16-D z (A1_z16, A2_z16, A3_z16) exist and reach the same verdict.

entries.claim: A small MLP probe reading the 64-D z of the proposed model recovers the R2 structure descriptor and the wrench profile about as well as the same probe reading the full 512-D dense map (structure retention, a mean over five quantities, 1.07 on TACO and 1.10 on ARCTIC; z is not above the dense-map probe on every quantity), while the probe reading r recovers little of it on average (0.03 on TACO; -0.53 on ARCTIC, i.e. worse than predicting the training mean), which supports that structure information is concentrated in z. The ratio has no interval, the probed quantities are the ones the relational teacher was built from, and one training seed was run.
entries.metric: Structure retention (dimensionless; higher = more structure information recoverable). A 2-layer MLP probe (hidden 256) is trained on frozen codes of the training frames and scored on the unique test frames (TACO 22 938, ARCTIC 11 560). For each of five quantities (part-participation AUPRC, amount R2, centroid error, normal angle, wrench explained variance) retention = (probe - trivial) / (dense-map probe - trivial); structure retention is the mean of the five. 1 = as good as the probe on the full dense map, 0 = as good as predicting the training mean, negative = worse than that. No interval is given for this ratio.

entries.claim_as_extracted: A small probe reading the 64-D z of the proposed model recovers the R2 structure descriptor and the wrench profile at least as well as the same probe reading the full 512-D dense map (structure retention 1.07 on TACO, 1.10 on ARCTIC), while the probe reading r recovers little of it on average (0.03 on TACO, -0.53 on ARCTIC), which supports that structure information is concentrated in z.
entries.correction_reason: Numbers are right. 'At least as well' holds only for the five-quantity mean: TACO centroid retention 0.996 and ARCTIC normal 0.945 are below 1. The retention ratio has no interval, and the unpaired 95 % intervals of the underlying probe metrics of z and of the dense map overlap for every quantity that has one on ARCTIC and for all but wrench EV on TACO (probe_metrics.csv lo / hi columns), so 107 % / 110 % should read 'about as well as', not 'more than'. -0.53 is worse than the trivial predictor, which 'little' hides.

entries.claim: In the proposed model, adding r to z lowers the test reconstruction error of the dense map from 0.449 to 0.151 on TACO and from 0.645 to 0.205 on ARCTIC (mean per-frame L2, lower is better): the L2 error falls by 66 % / 68 %, and the squared error that z alone leaves falls by 73 % / 87 %. r therefore carries complementary dense detail that z does not reconstruct; that detail is a small part of the map (z alone already explains 98.4 % / 95.7 % of its variance).
entries.metric: E = mean over the unique test frames (TACO 22 938 frames of 186 takes; ARCTIC 11 560 of 44 takes) of the L2 distance between the reconstructed and the true 512-point contact map, in raw contact units (map values in [0, 1]); lower is better. E_zonly uses the z-only map, E_full the z + r map, both of the same model A3. Gain_r = (E_zonly - E_full) / E_zonly (relative reduction of the L2 error). explained_by_r = 1 - sum of squared errors (z + r) / sum of squared errors (z only) (share of the z-residual energy removed). Brackets = 95 % take-cluster bootstrap interval, 1000 resamples (test-set uncertainty, not training variance).

caveats: Two different quantities: Gain_r 0.66 / 0.68 is the reduction of the L2 error; 73 % / 87 % (explained_by_r) is the reduction of the squared error (energy). Do not write 'r removes 73 % of the error'.

The part r completes is small: the 64-D z alone already explains 98.4 % (TACO) / 95.7 % (ARCTIC) of the standardised map variance, so 'r matters' concerns the 1.6 % / 4.3 % that z leaves (report Sections 7 and 13: at |z| = 64 the premise of a large residual is weak by construction).

The plain autoencoder A0 is a weak control (collapsed latent, effective rank 3.4 / 3.3 of 128; worse than linear PCA-128, sanity warning 01); the report names linear PCA-128 the stricter reference. On TACO the z-only map (0.449) is worse than PCA-128 (0.353); on ARCTIC it is better (0.645 vs 0.760).
The correction acts on the contact patches (about 98 % of the z-residual energy lies on points with GT contact >= 0.05); r adjusts amplitude and fine shape of patches that z places.
The TACO interval of explained_by_r is wide ([0.64, 0.83]).
One training seed; intervals are test-set uncertainty. Most runs had their best validation step at the last evaluation (sanity check 11), so absolute errors are not converged values.
The ARCTIC validation takes are harder than its test takes for every model (A3 val 0.310 vs test 0.205).
entries.claim_as_extracted: In the proposed model, adding r to z lowers the test reconstruction error of the dense map from 0.449 to 0.151 on TACO and from 0.645 to 0.205 on ARCTIC (a 66 % / 68 % lower L2 error, 73 % / 87 % of the squared error that z alone leaves), so r carries complementary dense detail that z does not reconstruct.
entries.correction_reason: Values and direction confirmed in reconstruction_metrics.csv (gain_r 0.664 / 0.682; explained_by_r 0.733 / 0.872). The parenthesis '73 % / 87 % of the squared error that z alone leaves' can be read as 'remains' instead of 'is removed'; state the verb. The size caveat (1.6 % / 4.3 % left by z; report Sections 7 and 13) must stay next to the number. Intervals are test-set bootstrap, one seed.

entries.claim: In latent swaps between structurally similar test frames, the structure of the decoded map follows the frame that supplied z in 97 % (TACO) and 98 % (ARCTIC) of swaps, whereas the transplanted dense detail follows the frame that supplied r in 77 % of swaps on TACO but only 44 % on ARCTIC, which is consistent with a preferential, not a complete, factorization.
entries.metric: Share of swaps (higher = cleaner role separation). Pairs (A, B) are test frames of the same mesh from different takes whose R2 + wrench teacher distance is in the lowest 20 % of that mesh's cross-take pairs and whose dense distance is above its median; each pair is swapped both ways (decode z of A with r of B and the reverse). 'Structure follows z' = the decoded map's R2 + wrench distance to the z donor is smaller than to the r donor. 'Detail follows r' = the cosine between the added correction and the r donor's own residual is larger than with the host's residual. Brackets = 95 % take-cluster bootstrap interval (1000 resamples, clustered on the z donor's take). Pre-registered thresholds 0.70 (structure) and 0.60 (detail).

caveats: The structure half is largely built into the architecture: the swapped map is the host's z-only map plus a small correction (swapping r moves the map by 14 % / 16 % of the distance between the two frames, report Section 10: 'a fine correction, never a change of structure'), so structure staying with the z donor is expected. The informative half is the detail half.

On ARCTIC the transplanted detail resembles neither the r donor's nor the host's residual (cosines 0.02 and 0.07, paired difference -0.04 [-0.07, -0.01]); the report reads r as a correction conditioned on the structure it is attached to. No experiment isolates the cause.

On ARCTIC the two frames of a pair differ in articulation and are structurally less similar to begin with (mean teacher distance 0.575 vs 0.503 on TACO), so 'the same detail on another structure' is less well defined there (report Sections 10 and 15).
Structure of a decoded map is extracted with the reference frame's ground-truth part labels (report Section 15).
The same split holds without the relational loss (A2: 96 % / 72 % on TACO, 92 % / 42 % on ARCTIC), so the swap result does not by itself show the effect of the relational loss.

One training seed; intervals are test-set uncertainty.

entries.claim: Read off frame by frame along real test trajectories, r is about as persistent as the dense residual it encodes (autocorrelation at 8 frames 0.65 vs 0.69 on TACO, 0.80 vs 0.77 on ARCTIC) and less persistent than z and than the plain autoencoder latent, so the results do not support treating r as a fixed sequence-level code.
entries.metric: Autocorrelation at lag h = 8 frames (30 Hz) of a code when the frozen encoders are applied frame by frame to the ground-truth test trajectories (TACO 364, ARCTIC 186 sequences of 64 frames; nothing temporal trained): sum over dimensions of Cov(x_t, x_t+h) / sum of Var(x); higher = the code changes more slowly; no interval in the table. Ridge R2: linear ridge regression fitted on training trajectories and scored on test trajectories, predicting a code 8 frames ahead (higher = more predictable). Displacement ratio: mean ||x_t+8 - x_t|| divided by the mean distance between random frames of different sequences, with a 95 % take-cluster bootstrap interval.

caveats: Correction to the page brief: 'its future is barely predictable beyond the current structure' rests on the gain 0.07 / 0.14, which is r2_from_both minus r2_from_current_z3; in the table r2_from_both (0.097 / 0.157) is lower than the R2 from r(t) alone (0.315 / 0.345), and the report prose 'from both 0.38 / 0.48' is not in the table. In eval_temporal.py the ridge penalty is scaled by the mean feature variance of the concatenated input while z has a far larger scale than r, so this gain is not a reliable measure. Supported wording: the current structure z linearly predicts almost none of r (R2 0.03 / 0.02), and r's own past predicts it only partly (ridge R2 0.31 / 0.34 against 0.69 / 0.76 for z; copy-forward 0.36 / 0.63).
'About as persistent as', not 'equal': r is slightly below the residual on TACO (0.65 vs 0.69) and slightly above on ARCTIC (0.80 vs 0.77).

The verdict 'partial' rests on the comparison with A0's plain latent h (0.65 vs 0.88; 0.80 vs 0.94), a control the report itself calls weak; on ARCTIC it is the only persistence criterion that fails, on TACO the gain criterion (the unreliable number) and, marginally, the displacement criterion (0.5448 vs 0.5369) fail too. The two reference-relative criteria were fixed after an untrained smoke run (report Section 3).
The hand-designed R2 + wrench descriptor has about the same autocorrelation as r (0.68 / 0.79), so a low value is not specific to the realization code.
Persistence is measured by frame-wise encoding and a linear ridge only; a temporal model over r might extract more (report Section 15). Autocorrelations have no interval.
r is still a real, non-collapsed code (effective rank 15.2 / 14.2 of 64): describe it as a per-frame realization residual / complementary dense detail, never as noise.
One training seed; one residual-decoder recipe.

One training seed.

caveats: One training seed per model; every interval is test-set (take-cluster bootstrap) uncertainty, not training variance.

The split is produced by the relational R2 + wrench teacher, not by the architecture alone: without it (A2) z retains 0.77 / 0.63 and collapses to an effective rank of 2.7 / 2.5; part of the structure then appears in r on TACO (0.30) and is simply lost on ARCTIC (r about 0).
The literal table answer to 'proceed to Stage 2?' is 'partial (Case B)'; 'Stage 2 is justified' is the wording of the index, not of the decision table.
The control A0 is weak, so the criterion 'A3 reconstructs about as well as A0' is met trivially (A3 is 75 % / 78 % below A0).
z's variance is concentrated in few directions (effective rank 6.5 / 8.0 of 64; sanity warning 06).
The z-neighbourhood margin over the dense map is small and the unpaired intervals overlap on both datasets; the rule compares point estimates only.

The teacher mixes R2 and the wrench profile half and half; an R2-only teacher was not run, so the wrench's contribution is not attributed (report Section 15). Wrench capability is a proxy for functional grasp capability.
Results exist for TACO and ARCTIC only; there is no OakInk2 result in this study.
entries.claim_as_extracted: By the study's pre-registered rule the outcome is Case B, partial factorization, on both TACO and ARCTIC: the z side (structure probes, reconstruction through z + r, z neighbourhoods) is supported, while the persistence of r is only partial on both datasets and the transfer of r's detail is only partial on ARCTIC.
entries.correction_reason: Cases and answers confirmed (experiment_config.json, decision_summary.csv, aggregate.py::decide). 'Pre-registered' is the project's own term for thresholds stored in cf_common.DECISION; there is no external registration and two of the four persistence criteria were fixed after an untrained smoke run (report Section 3), so 'fixed in advance' is safer. 'Transfer only partial on ARCTIC' softens a failed threshold: 'partial' is the label of the two-part swap question. The neighbourhood 'yes' compares point estimates only (intervals of z and dense map overlap on both datasets).

dataset_differences: Swap, detail half: the transplanted dense detail follows the r donor in 77 % [72, 82] of swaps on TACO but 44 % [39, 50] on ARCTIC (threshold 60 %); detail cosine to the r donor vs to the host 0.44 vs 0.11 on TACO, 0.02 vs 0.07 on ARCTIC (paired difference +0.33 vs -0.04). Rule answer to the swap question: yes on TACO, partial on ARCTIC.
Swap, structure half: 97 % (TACO) and 98 % (ARCTIC), similar on both; the ARCTIC pairs are structurally less similar to begin with (mean teacher distance 0.575 vs 0.503) and differ in articulation.
Structure in r: retention 0.03 on TACO (participation 0.65 and normal 0.34 still recoverable) versus -0.53 on ARCTIC (probe worse than the training-mean predictor; amount retention -2.1).
Structure in z: 1.07 (TACO) and 1.10 (ARCTIC); the quantity on which z is below the dense-map probe differs (centroid on TACO, normal on ARCTIC).

Reconstruction: absolute errors are higher on ARCTIC (z only 0.645, z + r 0.205) than on TACO (0.449, 0.151); r removes a larger share of the z-residual energy on ARCTIC (87 % [86, 89]) than on TACO (73 % [64, 83], wide interval); z alone leaves 4.3 % of the map variance on ARCTIC and 1.6 % on TACO.
References: on TACO the z-only map (0.449) is worse than linear PCA-128 (0.353); on ARCTIC it is better (0.645 vs 0.760). The plain autoencoder A0 is weaker on ARCTIC (0.944) than on TACO (0.609).

Persistence of r: autocorrelation at 8 frames 0.65 on TACO and 0.80 on ARCTIC; relative to the dense residual it is slightly lower on TACO (0.65 vs 0.69) and slightly higher on ARCTIC (0.80 vs 0.77). TACO misses three of the four persistence criteria (one marginally, one on an unreliable number), ARCTIC misses one; both get 'partial'.
Copy-forward R2 of r eight frames ahead: 0.36 on TACO, 0.63 on ARCTIC (ridge self-prediction 0.31 / 0.34).
What stops Case A: TACO 'not yet: r persistence'; ARCTIC 'not yet: swap, r persistence'. Both are Case B.
Without the relational loss (A2): on TACO part of the structure moves into r (z 0.77, r 0.30); on ARCTIC it is lost from both codes (z 0.63, r about 0).

Data: TACO 22 938 unique test frames from 186 takes, swap pairs over 40 rigid-object meshes; ARCTIC 11 560 test frames from 44 takes, 11 articulated objects. ARCTIC validation takes are harder than its test takes for every model (A3 val 0.310 vs test 0.205).
OakInk2: no result exists for this study; TACO and ARCTIC only.
do_not_claim: z and r are disentangled / independent. The model has no independence term, E_r and D_r both read z, and the report states the claim is role separation, not disentanglement.

The network discovered the structure / realization boundary by itself. z is taught by a relational R2 + wrench teacher; the same architecture without it (A2) gives a collapsed z with retention 0.77 / 0.63. The block title 'discovers the boundary' overstates this.
z contains more information than the dense map (from 107 % / 110 %). The number is relative to a small probe on the 512-D map, and the probed quantities are the ones the teacher was built from.

r contains no structure, or r is noise. On TACO the r probe recovers part participation well above the trivial predictor; r has an effective rank of about 15 of 64 and removes 73 % / 87 % of the z-residual energy. Call it a realization residual / complementary dense detail.
r is 'anti-structural' on ARCTIC. The negative retention is a probe that is worse than the training mean; the report reads it as overfitting.
r removes 73 % / 87 % of the reconstruction error. That is the squared-error (energy) share; the L2 error falls by 66 % / 68 % (Gain_r).

The swap test shows the model learned that structure lives in z. Structure following z is largely by construction (z-only map plus a small correction that moves the map by 14 % / 16 % of the pair distance); the same 92-96 % appears without the relational loss.
r's detail transfers between frames. It does on TACO (77 %) but not on ARCTIC (44 %); never state the transfer without the dataset.
Articulation causes the ARCTIC transfer failure. The report offers this as a reading; no experiment isolates it.
r is a persistent or sequence-level identity, or a fixed code per grasp. The persistence question is answered 'partial' on both datasets and r tracks the dense residual frame by frame.

r's future is barely predictable beyond the current structure (gain 0.07 / 0.14), or 'from both 0.38 / 0.48'. The gain rests on a joint ridge fit that scores below the fit from r alone in the same table, and 0.38 / 0.48 is not in any table.
r is unpredictable. Its copy-forward R2 eight frames ahead is 0.36 (TACO) / 0.63 (ARCTIC) and only a linear ridge was tried.
The factorization is 4 x better than a standard autoencoder, without saying that A0 is a weak control with a collapsed latent and that linear PCA-128 is the stricter reference (2.3 x / 3.7 x).
r is a large part of the contact map. z alone already explains 98.4 % / 95.7 % of the map variance.
The result is robust to training randomness. One seed per model; every interval is test-set bootstrap uncertainty.
Stage 1 fully justified Stage 2, or Case A. The table answer is 'partial (Case B)'.
The models were trained to convergence or from scratch. Most runs had their best validation step at the last evaluation, and the primary A2 / A3 phase B started from an earlier 16 000-step z branch.
The finding holds on OakInk2 or across datasets in general. Only TACO and ARCTIC were run, separately.

z captures human intent, or the wrench term makes z functional by itself. The wrench profile is a proxy for functional grasp capability, mixed half and half with R2 in the teacher; its separate contribution was not tested.
z-space neighbourhoods are clearly more structural than dense-map neighbourhoods. The margin is small and the unpaired intervals overlap on both datasets.

candidate_images.caption: Reconstruction of single test frames by the proposed model (TACO top three rows, ARCTIC bottom three). From left: true contact map, map decoded from z alone, the correction added through r (red = more contact, blue = less; scale -0.3 to +0.3), and the full z + r map; each dot is one of the 512 canonical surface points of the object, shown in a 2-D projection. z alone already places the contact patch; r adds a small local correction on that patch. Frames are the median-residual frame of each of the three most frequent test objects per dataset.
